subject.title: fix(cron): honor AbortSignal in waitForActiveCronTaskRuns poll

question: Should a superseding gateway restart be allowed to interrupt cron task-drain waiting, and what cleanup/state guarantee must hold before the subsequent restart continues?
rationale: The codebase needs an owner-defined restart-coalescing contract; an independently created one-second timeout cannot determine which lifecycle event is safe to treat as cancellation.

options.title: Define and wire superseding restart cancellation
options.body: Specify the restart-coalescing owner and pass its real abort signal into the drain wait, with an end-to-end test that proves the earlier restart is interrupted safely.

options.title: Keep the existing bounded drain deadline
options.body: Remove the same-deadline signal plumbing and retain the current one-second drain behavior until a concrete lifecycle-cancellation requirement is approved.

recommendation.title: Keep the existing bounded drain deadline
recommendation.body: Remove the same-deadline signal plumbing and retain the current one-second drain behavior until a concrete lifecycle-cancellation requirement is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: A history-based owner could not be established because read-only command execution was blocked before the required blame and log pass.
